nodes.name: Ni foam electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: The copper foil substrate (1×2.5 cm) was polished by sandpapers, and then ultrasonicated in water and ethanol for 5 min sequentially. The electrolyte was prepared by adding 0.26 M NiCl2·6H2O into 1.5 M NH4Cl solution prepared with DI water. The deposition voltage was 12 V, and the deposition time was 50 s using a copper foil and a graphite rod as working and counter electrodes, respectively, with a DC power supply.
nodes.source_text: The electrolytes for Ni, Fe, and Co foams were prepared by adding 0.26 M NiCl2·6H2O, FeSO4·7H2O, and CoSO4·7H2O into 1.5 M NH4Cl solution... The deposition voltage was 12 V, and the deposition time was 50 s.

nodes.name: NiCo foam electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: The copper foil substrate (1×2.5 cm) was polished by sandpapers, and then ultrasonicated in water and ethanol for 5 min sequentially. The electrolyte was prepared by using NiCl2·6H2O + CoSO4·7H2O to prepare electrolytes with total metal concentration of 0.26 M. The deposition voltage was 12 V, and the deposition time was 50 s using a copper foil and a graphite rod as working and counter electrodes, respectively, with a DC power supply. The deposition efficiency was determined to be 41.93%.
nodes.source_text: For the synthesis of bimetal NiCo and NiFe foams, we used NiCl2·6H2O + CoSO4·7H2O... to prepare electrolytes, respectively, and the total metal concentration was 0.26 M. Other preparation procedure was the same... The deposition efficiency of NiCo... were determined to be 41.93%

nodes.characterization_summary: NiCo foam possesses a unique 3D porous foam mesostructure with an average cavity diameter of ~15 um, assembled by nanoparticles. NiFe foam exhibits similar 3D porous foam structure with smaller pore size.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 2a, the NiCo foam possesses a unique 3D porous foam mesostructure, with an average cavity diameter of ∼15 um. ... The SEM images (Fig. 2c-d) of NiFe foam exhibit a similar 3D porous foam structure with smaller pore size.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS elemental mapping reveals Ni/Co and Ni/Fe elements are homogeneously distributed across the nanoparticles in NiCo and NiFe foams. Atomic ratios of Ni:Co and Ni:Fe are 1:2 and 1:1.36 respectively.
nodes.evidence_snippet: EDS elemental mapping in Fig. 2e-1 further clearly reveals that Ni/Co and Ni/Fe elements are homogeneously distributed across the nanoparticles ... According to the EDS elemental analysis (Fig. S1), the atomic ratios of Ni to Co and Ni to Fe are further determined to be around 1:2 and 1:1.36

nodes.characterization_summary: NiCo foam contains metallic Ni and Co phases. NiFe foam demonstrates components of Ni₃Fe and Fe.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. S3a, with the increasing of Co ratio in the NiCo foam, the peak intensity of Ni becomes weaker, and the Co peaks become stronger, confirming the presence of metallic Ni and Co phases in the NiCo foam ... Similar results are also revealed on the NiFe foam ... which demonstrates two components of Ni₃Fe and Fe.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni 2p spectroscopy of Ni foam shows Ni 2P1/2 at 873.5 eV and Ni 2P3/2 at 856.0 eV (Ni2+), Ni(0) at 852.5 eV. NiCo foam Ni 2p peaks shift positively; Co 2p peaks shift negatively by 0.35-0.50 eV due to Ni-Co interaction. NiFe foam Ni 2p shifts positively; Fe 2p shows Fe3+ as main valence.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In Fig. 3c, the Ni 2p spectroscopy of Ni foam exhibits typical spin-orbit doublet peaks of Ni 2P1/2 (873.5 eV) and Ni 2P3/2 (856.0 eV), which are typical peaks of Ni2+ due to surface oxidation. ... For NiCo foam, the two spin-orbit doublet peaks exhibit a positive shift ... the two spin-orbit doublet peaks of Co 2p display a negative shift of 0.35 eV for Co 2P3/2 and 0.50 eV for Co 2P1/2 ... For NiFe foam, the two doublet peaks of Ni 2p show a positive shift ... the Fe 2p spectrum of Fe foam shows two typical doublet peaks at 710.9 eV and 724.4 eV ... confirming higher average valence states of Fe in NiFe foam.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman during OER on NiFe foam shows formation of Ni/FeOOH active species starting at 1.425 V vs RHE. Ni foam forms β-NiOOH at 1.625 V (475, 556 cm⁻¹). Fe foam shows Fe₂O₃ at 295 cm⁻¹ from 1.025 V and FeOOH at 582 cm⁻¹.
nodes.evidence_snippet: NiFe foam is able to produce a large amount of Ni/FeOOH active species starting at a low potential of 1.425 V (Fig. 5k) ... For the Ni foam ... it splits into two obvious peaks at about 475 and 556 cm⁻¹, corresponding to two characteristic bands of β-NiOOH ... For the Fe foam ... an obvious peak at 295 cm⁻¹ originated from Fe-O vibration in Fe₂O₃ shows up under a low potential of 1.025 V ... a broad peak appears at about 582 cm⁻¹, which corresponds to the FeOOH phase.

nodes.characterization_summary: Double-layer capacitance Cdl values: Co foam 25.75 mF cm⁻², NiCo foam ~17.17 mF cm⁻² (1.5× less than Co), Ni foam ~5.65 mF cm⁻² (4.56× less than Co).
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 4e, unexpectedly, not the NiCo foam but the Co foam shows the largest Cdl of 25.75 mF cm⁻², which is almost 4.56 times that of Ni foam and 1.5 times that of NiCo foam
